hierarchy.rule: Core reviewers are anchors. Auxiliary judgments are independent supporting evidence and never equal-status votes.

normal_auxiliary_policy.strong_support_definition: At least 80% of at least five valid eligible Auxiliary judgments select the same category.

case_policy.core_exact_agreement: Keep provisionally. Auxiliary disagreement creates a warning; reopen only when strong eligible Auxiliary support is at the opposite extreme, NO versus CLEAR. Never auto-override.
case_policy.core_NO_vs_PLAUSIBLE: Auxiliary support may prioritize targeted re-review or later inform the adjudicator. It cannot determine the category.
case_policy.core_PLAUSIBLE_vs_CLEAR: Treat as a calibration/intensity candidate. Auxiliary support is context only and cannot determine the category.
case_policy.core_NO_vs_CLEAR: Always manual targeted re-review and, if persistent, independent adjudication. Auxiliary majority is never sufficient.
case_policy.one_core_missing: Do not substitute Auxiliary for the missing Core. Complete the missing Core judgment after guide freeze or keep unresolved.
case_policy.reviewer2_invalid_tail: Do not treat Auxiliary as Core-2 replacement. Obtain real Reviewer-2 judgments after guide freeze.

AUX_R06.method: Pairwise-complete analysis per cell and explicit valid denominator. Missing values stay missing; no imputation and no global downweight.
AUX_R06.reason: The small coverage gap is not evidence of poor judgment quality.

AUX_R08.allowed_use: Preserve unchanged and report as a separately labeled sensitivity perspective.
AUX_R08.prohibited_use: Do not include in strong-support thresholds, consensus counts, majority summaries, Core overrides, or automatic adjudication.
AUX_R08.reason: Near-total avoidance of NO makes the scale non-comparable with both Core anchors and the other Auxiliary reviewers; its inclusion would mechanically bias support toward PLAUSIBLE/CLEAR.
